summary: The probe is sound and would give a clear reading, but neither reading can change a decision that is open right now. The rewrite it is meant to inform (triton-flash-decode-full-paired-kv: paired 128-byte rows plus about 2 waves of CTAs) is already running and covers both levers, and decode has 4 checks left. Re-queue it only if that rewrite's stage 1 fails to beat FA3's own kernel time on full decode.
justification: A. The mechanism is now correct. Under varlen dynamic split an explicit num_splits only caps the split count (min(dynamic, static)), so num_splits=1 does bind: the grid becomes B*h_k CTAs (64 at B=32, 32 at B=16, 2 at B=1) with no partials and no combine. Dropping scheduler_metadata on decode is needed for the cap to apply; it adds an in-call prepare launch of about 2 us, which is small next to the expected moves. The readings are interpretable. At B=32 the CTA count halves and at B=16 it drops 4x, which gives two points against the same 128-CTA base. If the time stays flat, the limit is the global memory system or the gather pattern. If it scales with 1/CTAs, the limit is per-CTA latency or memory-level parallelism. One correction to the premise: the 491.6 us / 1.33 TB/s figure is from the older profile 5755a412. The current best profile (2b1f82408ab64116) shows full-layer FA3 at 374.4 us for decode_32, 188.8 us for decode_16 and 374.0 us for verify_32, which is a uniform ~1.75 TB/s at about 128 CTAs. Readings must use the same-run base rows, not the number in the hypothesis. The expected table is consistent with TASK's full-shape weights. Decode_1 and verify_1 full will lose roughly 10x on an 18-19 us kernel (+150-170 us on a ~184-240 us shape), so the headline drops heavily, as the hypothesis already concedes. Weakest link: decision value, not the physics. Both outcomes argue for the design already running. Pattern-bound means fetch both heads' 128-byte row, which the rewrite does. MLP-bound means oversubscribe with more splits, which the rewrite also does (S=9 at B=32, 17 at B=16). Neither outcome settles trtllm-decode-full-attention either. So a check spent here buys a diagnosis whose only consumer is a contingency, a rewrite stage 1 that underperforms, that has not happened yet. Also, 'flat' does not cleanly separate 'gather pattern' from 'HBM/L2 sector inefficiency of 64-byte head rows', since both are global limits. That matters little because the rewrite targets both.
confounders: marlin-block-m-cap-16: touches only the two Marlin MoE GEMMs, which run after attention on the main stream. It shares no launch, traffic or numerical path with the FA3 call. On full verify_16/32 it changed Marlin time, so compare those rows against the current best's same-run base, not older FINDINGS rows. It is not a confounder of the FA3 delta itself.

sglang-pipeline-parity-router-hilo-m8: its FA3 call is byte-identical to baseline.py, and its router change runs on the side stream after the o projection. It cannot cause or mask an FA3 split-count effect.
interference: No ab-revert or ab-tune is needed, because nothing landed touches the attention call. A control (num_splits=2 as a second point) would sharpen the curve, but it doubles the cost of a probe whose value is already conditional. The run disambiguates itself well enough: the sliding rows are an untouched control, and the full decode and verify rows give CTA ratios of 2x (B=32) and 4x (B=16). The blocker is not ambiguity. It is that the result cannot change today's decisions while the running rewrite answers the practical question directly: does paired-row, oversubscribed decode beat FA3's kernel time? A cheaper diagnostic is also already in flight, since the rewrite's own profile gives achieved TB/s at S=9/17 with 128-byte rows, a direct data point on both levers.
rules_flags: No rule problem found. num_splits=1 comes from config only, every key is still attended, there is no host sync, and dropping the judge's scheduler_metadata moves work into the timed call rather than out of it. The single-pass softmax with no fp32 combine is numerically at least as good.
Check-run only: it must never be promoted or used as a submit, because it is expected to regress decode_1/verify_1 full by ~10x in FA3 time.
The 1M-context full verify test (B=1, q_len=8) runs on 2 CTAs over 8192 key tiles. That should take a few ms, but confirm it stays inside the per-test budget.
open_questions: Re-queue trigger: if triton-flash-decode-full-paired-kv stage 1 is correct but its kernel time on full decode_16/32 does not beat FA3's 188.8/374.4 us, run this probe (num_splits=1, optionally plus num_splits=2) to learn whether the stage 2 fix is more in-flight parallelism or a different access pattern.
Before any re-queue, read the rewrite's profile. Achieved TB/s at S=9 (B=32) and S=17 (B=16) with 128-byte rows may already answer the gather-vs-MLP question at no quota cost.

Confirm from the judge's sgl_kernel FA3 source or version print that num_splits=1 with scheduler_metadata=None takes the non-split path (no FlashAttnFwdCombine) and is accepted together with cache_seqlens.

The hypothesis quotes decode_32 full FA3 at 491.6 us (profile 5755a412), but the current best shows 374.4 us. Update the expected 'why' text before any re-queue so the flat/2x thresholds are read against ~374 us.
